The check in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/v1.16.3/op-devstack/sysgo/l2_el_p2p_util.go#L53-L64 is failing for presets containing mixes of `op-geth/op-reth` nodes or several `op-reth` nodes.

topIssues.title: lokahi: Rust multi-chain interop node (tracking)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Tracking issue for **lokahi** (Hawaiian *lōkahi*: unity/agreement) — the Rust multi-chain interop node built from kona-node components at `rust/lokahi/`, mirroring op-supernode's protocol behavior (timestamp-lockstep cross-safety, deposits-only replacement, superroot/syncStatus) with a different architecture: per chain, a **ChainController** (kona's EngineActor, extended) as hub with derivation/gossip/sequencer spokes; cross-chain, one **interop actor** whose cross-safe promotions are the only way the FCU safe label moves. op-supernode is not replaced — lokahi is additive and wire-compatible with existing supernode RPC consumers.

Design docs (Notion, under 🌴 Lokahi): [Architecture Brainstorm](https://app.notion.com/p/3c1f153ee16281cfaa08dde809fb6c0d) · [Implementation Plan](https://app.notion.com/p/3c1f153ee162815ebf8ef132c161b518)

Phases (sub-issues; each phase carries its work items as sub-issues — dependencies are named per item so parallel work is visible):
- Phase 0: #22519 — delete op-supervisor-era interop legacy from kona (in progress)
- Phase 1: #22520 — kona shared-component refactors
- Phase 2: #22521 — lokahi N-chain scaffolding (no interop)
- Phase 3: #22522 — interop actor, cross-safe happy path
- Phase 4: #22523 — invalidation
- Phase 5: #22524 — RPC parity, sequencing, test harness

Broadly parallelizable from the start: #22529 (metrics label), #22531 (multi-chain L1 watcher), #22534 (kona-interop rules), #22535 (interop stores), #22539 (op-reth reorg spike).

🤖 *Co-created with Claude (Fable 5)*

topPRs.author: lucasmt
topPRs.body:
<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

An abstract model of the OP Supernode implemented in the Dafny language. Critical properties of the Supernode design have been formally verified in the model using Dafny's formal verification capabilities, including core invariants, cross-validity of `VerifiedDB` entries, and recovery of database consistency after successful pending transition application. Also includes a report produced by an AI-based analysis checking the model specifications over the Go code.

**Tests**

No tests have been added since there were no changes to the Go code, and the Dafny model has been formally verified.

topPRs.title: op-supernode: add formally verified Dafny model
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Description

This republishes #21820 from a repository-owned branch, rebased onto the latest `develop`, so maintainers can update the branch and CI can run against the current tree.

The original change adds an abstract OP Supernode model implemented in Dafny. It formally verifies critical design properties, including core invariants, cross-validity of `VerifiedDB` entries, and recovery of database consistency after successful pending-transition application. It also includes an AI-assisted analysis report comparing the model specifications with the Go implementation.

## Commit preservation

All 10 commits from #21820 were replayed in their original order with the original author attribution. `git range-diff` reports an exact patch match for every commit.

## Why

The source branch for #21820 is 836 upstream commits behind and has maintainer edits disabled, so it cannot be updated by repository maintainers. Rebasing the same commits onto current `develop` also incorporates the CI workflow changes made since its last run.

## Validation

- Rebase onto current `develop` completed without conflicts.
- `git range-diff` matched all 10 original commits one-for-one.
- The final diff contains only the original seven files under `op-supernode/dafny-models/`.
- No Go code changed.
- The Dafny CLI is not installed in the local environment, so the model was not re-verified locally.

Original PR and authorship: #21820 by @lucasmt.

topPRs.title: rust: update reth to v2.5.0 and drop the op-rs fork
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Moves the reth pin from the OP fork `op-rs/reth@aef8d3ef` back to upstream `paradigmxyz/reth`, `tag = "v2.5.0"`.

**The fork is droppable.** Its branch is upstream `f2eecc65` plus exactly one cherry-pick, `aef8d3ef92 feat(trie): expose payload state root receiver`. That patch is byte-identical (modulo blob hashes and line offsets) to upstream `92cf59e2be`, and `92cf59e2be` is in v2.5.0. `f2eecc65` is an ancestor of v2.5.0. So the fork carries nothing unique and the pin goes back to upstream.

Stacked on #22477 — this branch still contains its two commits, so review only `rust: update reth to v2.5.0 and drop the op-rs fork`.

## Shared versions

Synced to what v2.5.0 pins: `revm` 41.0.0 → 42.0.1 (subcrates 42.0.0), `revm-inspectors` 0.41 → 0.42, `alloy-evm` 0.37.0 → 0.38.0, alloy core 1.6.0 → 1.6.1, the alloy main family 2.1.1 → 2.3.0, published reth-core crates 0.5.0 → 0.6.0. All four lockfiles refreshed; no unrelated git-source drift.

## Upstream churn worth reviewing closely

**revm 41 → 42 is a major, not a routine bump.** It reworks the whole `Handler` gas pipeline around `GasTracker` and the EIP-2780 runtime gas phase, so `OpHandler::last_frame_result` is a genuine re-derivation, not a signature patch. The new body settles the frame with upstream's `handle_reservoir_remaining_gas` and applies the pre-Regolith deposit rules on top of the settled result; the EIP-8037 create refund is now upstream's `FrameResult::refundable_state_gas`, which reads a recorded `charged_create_state_gas` flag instead of inferring the condition.

**A mirror had genuinely drifted.** op-revm's `ExecuteEvm::replay` is a `copy` of upstream's `Evm` impl; upstream added an error path that finalizes the journal so a failed transaction does not leak into the next one, and our copy did not have it. Same class as the SDM warm-set leak (#21723). Fixed.

**Trie: `wiped` no longer derived from account status.** reth's `HashedStorage::from_bundle_state` stopped setting it (paradigmxyz/reth#26524); `HashedPostStateProvider::hashed_post_state` now owns destroyed-account handling and returns `ProviderResult`. Two OP consequences:
- `isthmus::withdrawals_root` builds its `HashedStorage` directly from the `BundleState`, bypassing `hashed_post_state`, so it keeps propagating `wiped` explicitly. Behaviour-preserving; `L2ToL1MessagePasser` is never destroyed in practice, but this is the withdrawals root, so it is preserved rather than dropped.
- `OpProofsStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state` now materializes the zeroed slots against the proofs storage at the parent block, mirroring upstream's `LatestStateProviderRef`.

**Behaviour change to confirm:** `ExecutionWitnessRecord`'s only public exit is now `into_execution_witness`, which also fills in ancestor headers. The payload-builder witness (`debug_executePayload`) therefore gained a headers provider and now returns headers, which it previously left empty. `debug_executionWitness` on the same server already returned them, so this makes the two consistent — but it is a response change, not just an adaptation.

**Flashblock log stream:** `ReceiptConverter` gained `RpcLog`/`convert_log` and the log-matching helpers convert through it. A flashblock is a payload, not a sealed block, so the header handed to the converter carries only the number, hash and timestamp the log fields need — exactly the values the old API took positionally. OP's `convert_log` is the identity.

Smaller compile-forced items: `from_reverts_auto` → `HashedPostStateSorted::from_reverts`, `ChangesetCache` → `reth_storage_overlay::OverlayManager`, `BuiltPayloadExecutedBlock::changed_paths` and `BuildNewPayload::{cache,state_root_handle}` removed, `validate_block_post_execution_with_hashed_state` gained a parent header (unused by OP), `calculate_initial_tx_gas` gained an EIP-2780 argument, `alloy_genesis::ChainConfig` gained `bogota_time`.

**Latent misdeclaration exposed:** kona-proof now declares `ark-bls12-381`'s `scalar_field` feature. It used to arrive by feature unification with revm-precompile, which moved to ark-bls12-381 0.6 — so `ark_bls12_381::Fr` stopped resolving with no change on our side.

## Mirrors

All 24 `UPSTREAM-MIRROR` tags re-verified against v2.5.0 / revm 42 / alloy-evm 0.38: 19 current, 5 frozen, none stale, `just mirrors --check` exits 0. Only two mirrors had actually moved upstream (`revm_handler::api`, `revm_handler::Handler::last_frame_result` — plus the mechanically-forced `refund`); the rest were verified unchanged. The frozen `DatabaseMetrics` port's recorded version moved from `rev:aef8d3e` to `rev:f2eecc6` so it names a commit reachable in the remote we now build against.

Two findings that are **not** fixed here, for a separate decision:
- `op-reth`'s `DEV_HARDFORKS` omits `EthereumHardfork::Osaka`, which upstream's dev list has had since before the old pin. Pre-existing drift, not introduced by this bump.
- That tag's prose claims the list "carries three Glacier forks upstream's does not" — neither list has them. The prose is wrong; left alone to keep this diff to the bump.

## Review (`reth-update-reviewer`)

Run per `.claude/skills/update-reth/SKILL.md`, following `docs/ai/reth-update-review.md`. It surfaced two HIGH findings; I verified both against upstream sources before acting.

**Fixed in the second commit — `MemoryOverlayOpProofsStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state`.** Same paradigmxyz/reth#26524 change as the Isthmus item above, landing in a place the first commit did not cover. Upstream turned `MemoryOverlayStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state` from a bare delegate into one that also zeroes destroyed accounts' slots from the *unpersisted* in-memory blocks; ours stayed a bare delegate, so only the persisted proofs storage got zeroed. Verified by diffing that function at `f2eecc65` (bare delegate) against `v2.5.0` (zeroing loop). It feeds `state_root_with_updates` in the proofs engine, so the symptom is a wrong state root. No compile error, no diff signal — exactly the class this review exists for.

**Reported, not fixed — the SP1 guest lost its patched SHA-256.** revm-precompile 42 moved `sha2` 0.10.9 → 0.11, and `[patch.crates-io]` only replaces the version it names. Verified in `rust/kona/sp1/programs/Cargo.lock`: before, only patched `sha2 0.10.9`; after, that **plus** an unpatched `sha2 0.11.0` whose sole consumer is `revm-precompile 42.0.1`. The SHA-256 precompile and the KZG versioned-hash check now run unaccelerated in the zkVM guest — a proving-cost regression, not a correctness one. The fix is a second patch entry, but only if `sp1-patches` publishes a sha2-0.11 tag; I have not confirmed one exists, so this needs an owner rather than a guess.

The reviewer also raised a set of medium/low items I did **not** act on — they are either pre-existing, inert today, or outside a dependency bump's scope. Listing them so they are not lost: engine persistence defaults moved upstream with no op-side override; kona's in-VM bn254 `ecAdd`/`ecMul` backend moved to ark 0.6; `ark-ff`'s `asm` feature lost the same way `scalar_field` was; c-kzg 2.1.7 → 2.1.8 under kona-host with the SP1 guest left on 2.1.7; `ChainConfig`'s new `bogota_time` absorbed by `..Default::default()` in superchain conversion; `OpSpecId::into_eth_spec` having no Amsterdam arm, so a future one-line edit would switch on EIP-2780 wholesale; and `eth_getMultiProof` arriving as a defaulted trait method on the OP namespace. Each wants its own issue rather than a rider on this PR.

On the deposit gas-cap exemption specifically, the reviewer disagreed with my "nothing changed" and was right to: revm 42 moved `initial_gas_and_reservoir` out of `Handler::execution` into a **new defaulted `Handler::tx_gas`** that op-revm does not override. The call site moved; it still reads `cfg().tx_gas_limit_cap()` and still runs inside the exemption window, so the behaviour holds — but it held by luck of a defaulted method landing inside the window, not by design. That is what the new tests pin.

## Verification

Run locally, exit codes observed:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo check --workspace --tests` (main) | 0 |
| `cargo check --workspace --tests` (op-rbuilder) | 0 |
| `cargo check --workspace --tests` (rollup-boost) | 0 |
| `just fmt-check` | 0 |
| `just lint` (fmt + clippy + docs + mirrors) | 0 |
| `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` | 0 — 2904/2904 passed, 11 skipped |
| `just test-docs` | 0 |
| `just check-no-std` | 0 |

The unit-test total is two runs: 2805 with `kona-sp1-proposer` excluded, then its 99 tests alone at `--test-threads 1`. Together they cover the same set; splitting was needed only because this box OOMs on the combined run.

Not run locally: op-reth E2E / acceptance suites, and anything needing a devnet.

## Judgement calls a human should confirm

0. **The SP1 sha2 patch loss above** — highest-consequence unfixed item; needs someone who knows whether an sp1-patches sha2-0.11 tag exists.
1. The `debug_executePayload` witness now includes ancestor headers (see above).
2. `isthmus::withdrawals_root` preserving `wiped` by hand rather than following upstream's zero-slots approach — the fail-safe reading, but it is a deliberate divergence from how upstream now expresses the same thing.
3. `OpBuilder::witness` / `OpPayloadBuilder::payload_witness` gained a headers-provider parameter and a `HeaderProvider` bound. Public API churn in op-reth.
4. `flashblock_receipts_stream` gained `BlockHeader = Header, Receipt = OpReceipt` bounds and yields `RpcLog<Rpc::Network>` instead of `Log` (identical for OP). It has no in-tree callers.
5. The SP1 guest workspace's declared `revm`/`alloy` versions were bumped too. `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` only tells you to refresh its lockfile, so those declarations had been lagging silently.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5*

topPRs.title: op-reth: add CLI surface snapshot test
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Josh Klopfenstein** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0A3E04GDMX/p1785194297744039?thread_ts=1785194297.744039&cid=C0A3E04GDMX)_

Replaces #22107, which GitHub auto-closed after a transient bad force-push to the branch (the branch is now clean; the diff below is the intended 3-file change).

## Before

op-reth inherits its entire CLI surface from the pinned upstream reth crates. A reth pin bump can add, remove, rename, or re-default operator-facing flags without producing any diff in this repository, so those changes ship silently and never get reviewed.

## After

A snapshot test renders the full op-reth command tree — every subcommand and every argument, including hidden ones, with aliases, value names, env vars, defaults, possible values, and help text — into a deterministic text file checked in at rust/op-reth/crates/cli/tests/snapshots/cli.snap. Any CLI surface change now fails the test and must be acknowledged by regenerating the snapshot, which makes the change visible in review:

    UPDATE_SNAPSHOT=1 cargo nextest run -p reth-optimism-cli --all-features cli_surface_snapshot

On mismatch the test prints the first differing line, prints the complete generated snapshot between BEGIN/END markers so it can be recovered verbatim from CI logs, and also writes it to the cargo target tmpdir.

## How

The renderer in rust/op-reth/crates/cli/tests/cli_snapshot.rs walks the clap command tree built by CommandFactory (the same tree the binary parses) and emits one line per argument in clap definition order. It is deliberately hand-rolled and std-only:

- It does not snapshot help output, which wraps at terminal width and varies by environment.
- It renders only the short help, never the long help — long help embeds registry-derived content such as the built-in superchain chain list on the chain flag, which would churn on registry updates unrelated to the CLI surface.
- Machine- and build-specific defaults are normalized to stable placeholders: defaults containing platform base directories (HOME, XDG dirs) and a small list of known build- or CPU-count-derived defaults (identity, builder.extradata, rpc.max-tracing-requests).
- No new dependency is added; the comparison and update logic (UPDATE_SNAPSHOT=1) is plain std. The workspace has insta available, but using it here would require touching the lockfile and would not print the full snapshot on failure, which the CI recovery loop below relies on.

A short section was added to rust/UPDATING-RETH.md telling reth bumpers the snapshot will surface upstream CLI changes and how to regenerate it.

## CI

The new test runs in the **rust-tests** CircleCI job (just test → cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features), which is part of the required-rust-ci gate. The test is gated on the crate dev feature because the dev-only test-vectors subcommand is part of the rendered surface; the --all-features run in CI enables it. Runs without that feature skip the test silently.

## Caveats

The committed snapshot is a best-effort construction generated offline from the pinned reth sources — this environment cannot compile the Rust workspace (the reth git dependency is not fetchable here), so the snapshot could not be produced by running the test. **The first CI run is expected to fail the new test**; the authoritative snapshot will be printed between the BEGIN/END markers in the rust-tests output, and a follow-up commit pastes it into rust/op-reth/crates/cli/tests/snapshots/cli.snap (or a local checkout runs the UPDATE_SNAPSHOT command above), after which the job goes green.

Refs #21687

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: extract observable proposer cycle
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Extract a crate-private proposer cycle while preserving the immediate first poll and configured production cadence.
- Separate work planning from spawning so each cycle can capture deterministic semantic diagnostics before workers start.
- Add typed task identities and completion results with one shared finalization path for production reaping and scenario settlement.
- Add test-only controls for direct ticks, exact task settlement, watchdog timeouts, and task-bound named barriers.

## Why

This is the next change in a series that makes the kona-sp1-proposer deterministically scenario-testable. Building on #22483, it makes one complete proposer cycle directly drivable and observable without changing proposer policy, production polling behavior, or the real asynchronous workers.

## Design notes

The snapshot is captured after completed tasks are reaped and new work is selected, but before new workers are spawned. Workers may finish immediately, so this boundary keeps observations deterministic while production still spawns the selected work in the same poll.

Task operation, class, target, and deduplication identity are represented separately because they answer different questions: proposal and reconciliation share one creation slot, proving is deduplicated per game, and resolution and claim sweeps are independent singletons.

Scenario controls are compiled only for tests. Exact settlement uses the same finalization path as production reaping, while named barriers and a watchdog make asynchronous tests deterministic without sleeps or a second task-lifecycle implementation

## Reviewer Consideration

Some tests call `sync_state()`, directly arrange the cached proposer state, and then invoke `cycle()`. These tests intentionally characterize post-sync orchestration, but they do not verify that the arranged state would be produced through the normal synchronization path.

A follow-up will introduce a stateful fake environment that scripts external inputs and drives these histories through normal ticks, covering the complete `sync -> reap -> plan -> snapshot -> spawn` sequence.


Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22171
